packs.title: Forms and Gardens
packs.promise: Explore architectural forms, park paths and old-city landmarks across Bangkok.

q.s: Collect three architectural forms at an art centre.
st: From a stopped position on open pavement, or in the guide photograph, find a curved edge, a narrow window opening and a broad wall surface.
Draw or describe the three forms. Read BACC’s architecture account and label its explanation as a sourced design idea, separate from what you can see.
Save your three forms and one comparison between the curved and straight edges. Leave artworks, signs and visitors out of your photographs.

q.s: Collect three reflections in a convention centre’s facade.
st: Choose an open stopped pedestrian position outside the building, or use QSNCC’s Front View gallery.
Find a repeated glass-panel grid, a reflection and a recessed entrance. Describe how the reflected view differs from the solid frame.
Save the three details with a small sketch or note. Do not enter an event, copy temporary signage or photograph visitors for the activity.

q.s: Create a small palette from a working flower market.
st: From a comfortable stopped position clear of trade, or in the guide photograph, choose three flower colours you can see. Do not touch or rearrange flowers.
Make a small three-colour palette with words, marks or a sketch. Invent a simple pattern that uses those colours without copying a seller’s arrangement.
Save the palette and pattern with one word for their mood. A note is enough; buying flowers or photographing people is unnecessary.

packs.title: River and Lanes
packs.promise: Find a Bangkok story in the details between the main street and the river lanes.

q.s: Write an unsent note from the details in front of you.
st: Choose a comfortable public-sidewalk view of the Grand Postal Building on Charoen Krung Road. No entry, postage or mailing is needed.
Notice one broad shape and one small repeated detail on the exterior.
Write a two-sentence postcard about your Bangkok day using both observations. Address it to yourself, or leave it unaddressed.

q.s: Build a close-up collection without touching a thing.
st: Choose a comfortable open public spot on Soi Wanit 2. This is a working neighborhood, so stay out of entrances and service space.
Find three outdoor building surfaces with different textures. Use walls, shutters and paving; avoid business stock, vehicles and religious objects.
Describe each texture in two words and arrange them from smoothest-looking to roughest-looking.

q.t: A Map Small Enough to Remember
q.s: Draw a route using details instead of street names.
st: Pause clear of traffic and doorways in the Talat Noi lanes.
Recall three details from your route: a corner, a material and a patch of open sky or water.
Draw an imaginary three-symbol memory map linking them, or describe the sequence in a field note. It is a keepsake, not directions for somebody else.
